history.period: 1872 CE (original Maula wooden pillar erected); 150th anniversary observed in 2022
history.summary: The Gorkha community's Durga temple in Shillong, dating to the British colonial era when Gorkha regiments were stationed in the Northeast. The first Gorkha Durga Puja in Shillong was organised in 1864 on the ground behind Bara Bazaar (with weapons installed instead of an idol - this site is now the seat of the Nepali Durga Mandir). The original Maula (sacred symbolic wooden pillar) was first erected in 1872 at the site of the present Cantonment School and later shifted permanently to the temple's current location; the temple celebrated 150 years of its inception in 2022. town_description: Shillong is the capital of Meghalaya, set in the East Khasi Hills at around 1,500 m above sea level. A former British hill station (capital of Assam from 1874 to 1972), it is known for its pine forests, colonial-era buildings, and busy markets like Police Bazar and Bara Bazar. It is the gateway to the Khasi Hills - Cherrapunji, Mawlynnong, and Dawki - and the state's main transport and commercial hub.
